title: Confirm phase-match tolerance stays as shipped
problem: The phase-matching tolerance decides whether a detected reflection 'belongs' to a phase. The board lists option (a) as owed to you, but the measurement is done and supports the shipped rule; the row only needs your yes.
context: Registered before the run (7f99ded, amended 3f828d5), Opus refuter. The shipped rule R0 = max(0.02 1/A, one detector pixel) lies inside every dataset's band: Thronsen 1.31 % mislabelled at 0.020, demo 97.0 % matrix, binned Al-Mg-Si 8.1 % not indexed (a fixed 0.02 would give 22.2 %), raw Al-Mg-Si 84.4 % matrix. Trap to avoid: at exactly one pixel (0.0190) Thronsen passes every T4 metric and at 0.0200 fails one (theta-prime speckle 7 > 5) - a two-speck margin on one dataset; picking 1 px for that would be tuning to the truth.

options.consequence: No number moves; the row closes.

options.label: (b) Pick a new rule (e.g. 3 px, which also passes all four bands)
options.consequence: Moves a shipped default on every dataset: Gate D, refuter, re-pin of every phase-map harness, for no measured gain.

recommendation: (a) - R0 is inside every band and no candidate is better everywhere; do not chase the two-speck T4 margin.

title: Read Si-SiGe.dm4 pattern size in GMS
problem: For DM4 files whose scan axes are stored fastest, the reader assumes each diffraction pattern is 480 tall x 448 wide. If Digital Micrograph actually stores it the other way, every pattern is transposed: strain axes swap and the R-Q rotation sign flips, silently. Si-SiGe is the strain reference dataset.
context: The 2026-09-05 fixture was generated from the code's own model, so it cannot catch this. The survey image (202 x 895 px = 17 wide x 77 tall) confirms DM writes x first for the scan pair; nothing in the commit justifies treating the detector pair differently. A two-minute check in GMS (Image Display Info: width/height of one pattern) settles it; a session then pins an ncempy checksum as the fixture and, if needed, flips DM4Reader.scanFastestStrides (:194).

options.label: You read width/height in GMS and reply with the two numbers
options.consequence: Two minutes; settles a possible silent axis swap on every scan-fastest DM4.

options.label: A session compares against the vendored py4DSTEM/ncempy reader only
options.consequence: Useful as the pinned fixture, but ncempy may share the same assumption; GMS is the authority.

options.label: Leave it
options.consequence: Strain and R-Q on DM4 stay possibly transposed; the parity run inherits the doubt.

recommendation: Both: you read GMS (authority), a session pins ncempy (fixture); it is the cheapest open science item on the board.
question: In GMS, is one Si-SiGe.dm4 diffraction pattern 448 wide x 480 tall, or 480 wide x 448 tall?
default_if_silent: The item stays open; the DM4 axis convention stays unverified.

title: Q calibration can pick the wrong shell
problem: Known-crystal Q calibration finds the innermost reflection ring and scales it to the crystal's first allowed reflection. If the ring it should use is missing (2H-WS2 on the basal zone: (0002) is invisible; the demo cube: the majority grain [001] has no {111}), it scales the wrong ring and stamps Q green 'Measured'. The S20 refuter caught the tool doing exactly this on the demo cube (Q 13.5 % low); the WS2 case (2.26x) was known. The night deferred the l-filter and the origin-gate statistic behind S14-D; the new finding says the same mistake may be live in the app.
context: The app already measures the shell ratio (AppState+ACOM.swift:113-129) and prints 'shell ratio 1.41 vs 1.155 predicted' or 'NOT self-checked' on the status line, then proceeds and marks Q green; thresholds to refuse were tried and refuted by Gate B. The advisor's candidate fix is threshold-free: assign the reference shell by matching the measured ratio sequence (sqrt3, 2, sqrt7 ...). Both a fix and the origin-gate statistic move shipped Q numbers (YELLOW). The S20 refuter asks for a check of whether the app's Calibration path can make the demo-cube mistake (now in open-items).

options.label: Keep both deferred; fund only the GREEN check + label: Q badge reads 'unchecked' when the shell ratio disagrees or only one shell exists
options.consequence: No number moves; the trust badge stops overstating on layered or single-zone cubes; a session verifies the app path on the demo cube.

options.label: Fund the threshold-free shell-assignment Gate D now
options.consequence: Moves Q on WS2/Mg/beta-double-prime-type cubes; needs S14-D's origins first (both read the same residuals).

options.label: Keep both deferred, no label
options.consequence: Q stays green on cubes where it is 13.5 % or 2.26x wrong.

recommendation: First option - the label is your 'unvalidated stays labelled' rule applied to Q, costs nothing, and the app-path check answers the S20 refuter's question.
question: Deferral stands (yes) - and fund the GREEN shell-ratio label plus app-path check now (yes/no)?
